facts.fact: A former National Population Commission director for Ondo State says only Commission staff, rural and urban, carry out digital registration, on Android personal digital assistants that need a stable network to upload, and that they revert to the manual process where the network or other problems prevent it; the platform is described as capturing records in real time. Undated, so the publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (e-CRVS) system

facts.fact: A mother in Ibadan, Oyo State, describes her newborn's registration at a health centre as entirely manual, written into a long paper register with a paper certificate issued, and a mother in Ilorin, Kwara State, took paper registration for her second child after the digital route failed on the network; neither is dated, so the publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (e-CRVS) system

facts.fact: The former Ondo State director says digital registration is for now available only for children under five, older ages still being registered manually and adults by attestation, which has also been digitised; the manual system is being phased out but not completely. Undated, so the publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (e-CRVS) system

facts.fact: The National Population Commission is making the transition from paper to electronic civil registration on a system the President launched in 2023 in partnership with UNICEF and other development partners; staff training in Ondo State is UNICEF-supported. The 2023 launch is the only date given, so the publication date is used.
facts.system: Electronic Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (e-CRVS) system
